segments.heading: Trial mode, lines 2095 to 2598: not run in the test
segments.text:
This comment line ends a block that bwx10 added. The block starts at line 2032.
- Every line from here to line 2598 belongs to the trial mode. `main` enters the trial mode only when an argument is the word `--trial` (lines 2912 to 2914). No argument line of the whole-chip test holds this word [Ref4]. So these lines did not run in the test.
- The self-test also calls some of these functions. It runs only with the option `--selftest` (line 2919), and no argument line of the test holds it [Ref4].
- Cross-check with the data: the trial mode prints rows that start with `M` before its first trial (line 2481). In the 9 csv files of the test every line starts with `I`, `T`, `P`, `C` or `#` (counted with awk on 2026-11-21) [Ref5].

segments.heading: Function `count_close`: closes the counter group (trial mode)
segments.text: Closes every counter file descriptor that `count_open` stored in `w->fd`. Each `close` that fails adds 1 to `w->close_fail`. Then it resets the group state of the worker: no leader, no open event, no failed open. `tev_add` (line 1924) records the step in the trace, and it does nothing without the option `--trace`.

segments.heading: Function `count_open`: opens the counter group (trial mode)
segments.text:
- The trial-mode version of `open_counters` (line 1582). The test uses `open_counters`, not this function.
- Lines 2119 to 2127 set up each counter in the same way as `open_counters`: one counter per event of `cfg`, user mode only, for the calling thread on any CPU. The first counter that opens is the leader of the group. The counters count from the open on.
- Different: it keeps every file descriptor in `w->fd`, so that `count_close` can close the group.
- Different: it writes nothing to stderr. An event that does not open adds 1 to `w->open_fail`. The error text of the first such event goes to `w->open_err`, and `emit_trial` prints it in an X row (a row that reports a problem).
- `group_open` becomes 1 also when no event opened.

segments.heading: Function `page_read`: page state before or after a trial (trial mode)
segments.text:
- Reads the page state of the one buffer of the worker into `r->pg[at]` with `read_smaps` (line 1515). Reads the four vmstat counters into `r->vm[at]` with `read_vmstat` (line 1545).
- `at` is 0 before the timed sequence and 1 after it. The timed sequence is the run of all windows of one trial (function `timed_sequence`, line 1995).
- The `# page_read` lines of the test files do not come from this function. `main` prints them at line 3118.

segments.heading: Function `switches`: context switches and page faults of the thread (trial mode)
segments.text:
Asks Linux for the resource use of the calling thread (`getrusage` with RUSAGE_THREAD). It stores three counts in the record `r` of the trial.
- `ru_nvcsw`: voluntary context switches. The thread stopped running by its own request, usually to wait for something.
- `ru_nivcsw`: involuntary context switches. Linux took the CPU away from the thread.
- `ru_minflt`: minor page faults. These are page faults that need no disk access. The first touch of a page is one.
- When the call fails, each of the three is stored as -1.

segments.heading: Function `first_multiplexed`: counters that did not count all the time (trial mode)
segments.text:
- A trial ends with `nwin` target windows (the windows of its last phase, see `trial_windows` at line 2217). `cnt` holds one counter reading per boundary of the target windows: `nwin` + 1 readings.
- For each target window the function compares the growth of the running time with the growth of the enabled time. It returns the number of the first window in which the running time grew less. In such a window the counters did not count all the time.
- It returns -1 when there is no such window.

segments.heading: Function `run_trial`: runs one trial, prints nothing (trial mode)
segments.text:
- Lines 2180 to 2183 put the counter group into the counter state of this trial. The counter state is the field `count` of a plan line: `closed`, `open` or `read`. For `closed` an open group is closed. For `open` or `read` a closed group is opened.
- Line 2184: the record keeps this state, or `fail` when counters are wanted and an event did not open.
- Lines 2185 to 2187 move the number of failed closes into the record and set the two failure counts of the worker to 0.
- Lines 2189 to 2197 prepare a check of the old read kernel. `old` is the last window of the trial whose kernel has the type T_OLDREAD. Every 8-byte word of the buffer holds `w->v`. So this kernel must return `w->v` times the number of words of its range. The sink is set to this value plus 1, so that a value from an earlier call cannot pass the check.

- Before the timed sequence: page state (`page_read`), context switches (`switches`), thread CPU time (`tcpu`, line 1945).
- Lines 2205 to 2209 run the timed sequence: `timed_sequence_hot` (line 2056) with the option `--hot-copy`, otherwise `timed_sequence` (line 1995). Line 2209 is the else branch of the `if` at line 2205. The clock reads that time the windows are inside these two functions.
- The third argument is 1 for the counter state `read`. Then the timed sequence also reads the counter group at the boundaries of the target windows.
- After the timed sequence: the same three readings in the reverse order.
- `sink_ok` becomes 1 when the sink holds the expected sum, 0 when it does not, and -1 when the trial ran no old read kernel.

segments.heading: Function `trial_windows`: number of windows of one trial (trial mode)
segments.text: A trial has up to four phases, in this order: previous activity (1 window), prefix (4 windows), predecessor (1 window) and target (`nwin` windows). The plan may leave out each of the first three. Then the field `k` of that part is -1. The function adds the windows of the phases that the trial has.

segments.heading: Function `window_bins`: bin storage of one target window (trial mode)
segments.text: Returns the number of bins that one target window can fill: the window length `win_ms` divided by 10 (rounded down), plus 2. The requested length of a bin is 10 ms (BIN_NS, line 1813). For a trial without bins it returns 0.

segments.heading: Function `set_windows`: fills the plan fields of the windows (trial mode)
segments.text:
- Goes through the four phases of a trial in the order of the run: previous activity, prefix, predecessor, target. It skips a phase that the plan leaves out.
- For each window it sets the kernel `k`, the phase, the window number `widx` inside the phase (from 0) and the range `size` in bytes.
- `passes` is the number of kernel calls between two clock reads: 8 MiB (CHECK_BYTES, line 130) divided by `size`, rounded down, and at least 1.
- `dur_ns` is the requested length of the window in ns. A target window gets `win_ms`. Every other window gets the time of its phase divided by the number of windows of the phase.
- A target window of a trial with bins gets its own part of the bin storage: `bin_cap` bins.

segments.heading: Function `alloc_records`: one memory block for all trial records (trial mode)
segments.text:
- Allocates one block of `recsz.bytes` bytes with `malloc`. It holds the records of all trials. `plan_trial` (line 2663) computed this size from the plan. Without memory the process ends with status 2.
- Fills the block with 0 (`memset`). Then it stores one byte in every page of the block and in its last byte, through a pointer to `volatile` data.
- The comment gives the reason for the extra stores: gcc joins `malloc` and `memset` into `calloc`, and `calloc` does not write a fresh block.
- Effect: every page of the block gets its first touch here, and not during a trial.

- Divides the block into arrays, in this order: the trial records (`rec`, one per trial), the window records, the counter readings, the bins, and with `--trace` the event log.
- The option `--rec-pad` moves the start of the window records by that many bytes (line 2278). The default is 0 bytes.
- The loop gives each trial its part of each array and calls `set_windows` for it. `nw` is the number of windows of the trial.
- Only a trial with the counter state `read` gets counter readings: `nwin` + 1 of them.

segments.heading: Function `print_s`: the S row of one trial (trial mode)
segments.text: Prints `S` and the 11 fields of the plan line of trial `i`, as text from the plan file. Then it prints the fields `cond` and `tgt` of the trial before it. For trial 0 it prints `none` two times.

segments.heading: Function `print_p8`: the P row of the trial mode
segments.text: Prints `P`, the trial number, the word `pre` or `post`, the two page values of the buffer in kB and the four vmstat counters. `print_na` (line 1562) prints `NA` for a negative value. The P rows of the test files have other columns: round, position, thread and buffer letter come first. Those rows come from `print_p` (line 1570), not from this function.

segments.heading: Function `emit_trial`: prints all result rows of one trial (trial mode)
segments.text:
- `g` is the index of target window 0 in the window list of the trial.
- P row `pre`: the page state before the timed sequence (`print_p8`).
- W rows, one per window: trial, phase, window number, kernel name, range size, bytes, start time and end time. The bytes are the range size times the number of kernel calls. The times are in ns since the process start.
- `max_gap` becomes the longest time between the end clock read of one window and the start clock read of the next window.
- B rows, one per bin of each target window: trial, window number, bin number, end time of the bin, bytes since the start of the window.
- The function prints bytes and times. It computes no rate.

- C rows, only for a trial with counter readings (counter state `read`): one row per target window. Each value is the difference of two readings. The first reading is taken before the start clock read of the window, the second after its end clock read.
- Columns of a C row: trial, window number, enabled time, running time, thread CPU time (all in ns), then one value per event.
- `NA` stands for the two times and for every event when no group is open or a group read failed in the trial. It also stands for an event that did not open.
- The C rows of the test files have other columns: round, position, kernel name, thread index and CPU come first. Those rows come from `main` (lines 3086 to 3103), not from this function.
- P row `post`: the page state after the timed sequence.
- X rows report problems, one row per kind. `coverage_na`: smaps has no exact entry for the buffer. `count_close`, `count_open` and `count_read`: a close, an open or a read of the counter group failed. `count_multiplexed`: the result of `first_multiplexed`. `sink`: the check of the old read kernel failed.

- E row, one per trial. The header (line 2478) names its columns. `wall_ns`: from the start of the first window to the end of the last window. `cpu_ns`: thread CPU time between the two `tcpu` calls of `run_trial`.
- The other columns of the E row: voluntary and involuntary context switches, the gap in ns between target window 0 and the window before it, `max_gap`, `sink_ok` and the counter state. `NA` stands for a value that could not be read or that the trial does not have.
- TR rows, only with `--trace`: one row per event of the trace, with its time in ns since the process start.
- `# trace_dropped`: printed when events did not fit into the trace. The trace keeps 1048576 events per trial (TRACE_CAP, line 1814).
- `# minflt`, only with `--trace`: the minor page faults of the worker between the two `switches` calls, or -1 when a reading failed.
- `fflush` writes the buffered rows to the output before the next trial starts.

segments.heading: Function `evict_step`: writes other memory before the first trial (trial mode)
segments.text:
- The comment describes the evict step of the option `--evict-mb N`. It gives the purpose: the lines of the benchmark buffer leave the caches, so the next read brings them back from memory.
- `evict_mb` holds N in MiB. `evict_t` holds the two clock readings around the step, and `evict_err` the text of an error.
- The comment lines `bwx11+` (2408) and `bwx11-` (2448) mark this text as added by bwx11.

- Reads the clock (`now_ns`, line 327). Maps `evict_mb` MiB of new anonymous private memory with `mmap`.
- Stores one 8-byte word at the start of every 64 B cache line of this memory, from the lowest address up. `i` counts 8-byte words, so `i += 8` is a step of 64 B. It does this 2 times over the whole range.
- `m` points to `volatile` data, so the compiler must keep every store.
- Unmaps the memory and reads the clock again.
- Returns 0. When `mmap` or `munmap` fails, it returns -1 and leaves the error text in `evict_err`.
- No timed window holds this step. `trial_worker` calls it once, before the first trial (line 2502).

segments.heading: Function `trial_worker`: the one worker thread of the trial mode
segments.text:
- Pins the thread to the one CPU of `--cpus` (`pin_cpu`, line 415). Then it asks Linux on which CPU it runs (`sched_getcpu`). If this is another CPU, the process ends with status 2.
- `w->v` is the value for every 8-byte word of the buffer: the process ID (`getpid`) plus 1, times a fixed 64-bit constant.
- Maps the buffer with `alloc_buf` (line 434). Line 2465 repeats the `madvise` request of `alloc_buf` only to learn its result (`madvise_ok`).
- First touch: the pinned worker writes the whole buffer once with `k_write` (line 531).
- `alloc_records` allocates the record block and touches every page of it.

- Lines 2470 to 2480 print the header: one `#` line with the column names for each row kind of the trial mode (S, P, W, B, C, E, X, TR). The first line still says `bwx8`, the version that added the trial mode.
- Lines 2481 to 2483 print M rows of the form `M,name,value`: the mode, the worker CPU, the CPU of the controlling thread (the thread of `trial_main`), the buffer size and the page policy (`madvise` or `nohugepage`). Then `madvise_ok`, CHECK_BYTES, and `aarch64` or `STAND-IN`.
- Lines 2484 to 2487: a checksum of the plan file, the number of trials, the sizes of the record block and whether the trace is on.
- Lines 2491 to 2495 (added by bwx10) print `rec_pad`, `hot_copy` and the size of one window record. They also print five addresses in hexadecimal: the record block, the first window record, the sink, the buffer and the worker structure.

- Evict step (added by bwx11): prints `M,evict_mb`. With a value above 0 it calls `evict_step`. On an error it prints an X row and the process ends with status 2.
- `M,evict_ns` is the time between the two clock reads of the step. It is 0 when no step ran. With a step and `--trace`, two TR rows give its start and its end.
- `M,pmu_type` and `M,events`: the counter settings, or `none`.
- One row `M,plan.<key>,<value>` for each pair of line 2 of the plan file.
- K rows, one per kernel that a trial of the plan uses: name, address of the function in hexadecimal, and this address modulo 64.
- An X row when the `madvise` request of line 2465 failed.

- The loop runs the trials in the order of the plan. Per trial it clears the trace, prints the S row (`print_s`), flushes the output buffer (`fflush`), runs the trial (`run_trial`) and prints the result rows (`emit_trial`).
- `run_trial` prints nothing. So the process writes no output inside a timed sequence.
- After the last trial it closes the counter group if it is open. It prints an X row when a `close` failed.

segments.heading: Function `plan_bad`: reports a defect of the plan file (trial mode)
segments.text: Writes `bad plan <file>, line <n>:` and a message to stderr. The message is built like a `printf` text from `fmt` and the arguments after it. Then the process ends with status 2.

segments.heading: Function `plan_long`: a whole number of the plan (trial mode)
segments.text: Accepts a text that holds decimal digits only and whose value lies from `lo` to `hi`. Then it stores the value in `*out` and returns 1. For any other text it returns 0. The caller then reports the defect with `plan_bad`.

segments.heading: Function `plan_size`: a size of the plan (trial mode)
segments.text: Accepts decimal digits with an optional capital letter `K`, `M` or `G` at the end (the number times 2^10, 2^20 or 2^30). The value must be above 0, and the size in bytes must fit into 64 bits. Then it stores the size in bytes in `*out` and returns 1. For any other text it returns 0.
